papers.title: Bioprinting dynamic hydrazone hydrogels via light-mediated crosslinking
papers.abstract: Viscoelastic hydrogels crosslinked by dynamic bonds hold great promise for mimicking the matrix dynamics of native tissues in cell culture and tissue engineering. Yet, their application in light-based bioprinting remains largely unexplored due to the incompatibility between reversible bond formation and photocrosslinking. This study addresses this key challenge by presenting a new class of photocrosslinkable, hydrazone-based bioinks developed from two modified polymers (Gel-A-DAAM and Gel-C-DAAM). These polymers are designed to enable reversible bond formation within hydrogel networks by attaching polymerizable groups to the polymer backbone via modular hydrazone conjugation chemistry. The resulting materials exhibit distinct mechanical properties depending on their hydrazide substituent, swelling medium, incubation temperature, and incubation time. Storage moduli of produced hydrogels vary between 0.08 - 1.2 kPa, which spans multiple scales of physiologically relevant tissue environments. The novel bioinks are suitable for droplet-based bioprinting followed by light-based crosslinking, and support cell spreading of human fibroblasts. Notably, the morphology of encapsulated cells varies with different hydrazide substituents, highlighting the potential of the developed bioink system to systematically investigate cell-matrix interactions. The combination of biological tunability and printability positions this system as a promising platform for fabricating next-generation tissue-mimetic constructs using advanced bioprinting technologies.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发可光交联的动态腙键水凝胶用于生物打印。
summary_zh.method: 通过修饰聚合物引入可逆腙键和光交联基团。

summary_en.motivation: To enable dynamic hydrazone hydrogels for light-based bioprinting by overcoming incompatibility between reversible bond formation and photocrosslinking.
summary_en.method: Two modified polymers (Gel-A-DAAM and Gel-C-DAAM) were synthesized with polymerizable groups attached via modular hydrazone conjugation chemistry.
summary_en.result: The hydrogels exhibited tunable storage moduli (0.08-1.2 kPa) and supported human fibroblast spreading with morphology varying by hydrazide substituent.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell encapsulation and droplet-based bioprinting followed by light crosslinking were performed.

papers.title: Timing and Trends of Periprosthetic Joint Infections Following Over 1,500,000 Primary and Revision Total Knee and Hip Arthroplasty Cases
papers.abstract: Background: Periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs) following primary and revision total knee arthroplasty (rTKA) and revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA) have been studied, but a contemporary large-scale analysis of incidence has not been performed. This study assessed PJI incidence and trends for TKA, THA, rTKA, and rTHA using a contemporary database. Methods: Epic Cosmos database was retrospectively queried (2015-2023). Current procedureal terminology codes identified patients: 27447 (TKA), 27130 (THA), 27486 (rTKA one component), 27487 (rTKA both components), 27134 (rTHA both components), 27137 (rTHA acetabular component), and 27138 (rTHA femoral component). PJI rates were identified using International Classification of Diseases 9/10 codes and analyzed using linear regression. Results: = .08). Conclusions: Significant PJI reduction after primary TKA and THA was observed over the last decade, but infection rates remained stable in revision cohorts. Further investigations are required to assess underlying reasons for observed PJI rate reductions following primary arthroplasty.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估近年全关节置换术后假体周围感染的发生率与趋势。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析2015-2023年Epic Cosmos数据库中的感染率。
summary_zh.result: 初次置换感染率显著下降，翻修组感染率稳定。
summary_zh.validation: 基于大规模临床数据库的统计分析。

summary_en.motivation: To assess contemporary incidence and trends of periprosthetic joint infections after primary and revision total knee and hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Retrospective query of the Epic Cosmos database (2015-2023) using CPT and ICD codes, with linear regression analysis.
summary_en.result: Significant reduction in PJI rates after primary TKA and THA over the last decade, while revision cohorts showed stable infection rates.
summary_en.validation: Large-scale clinical database analysis with statistical regression.
